CHECK THE WORDS. CONFIRM THE FIELDS.

Review extracted instructions

Compare each suggestion with its source. Check the confirmation box only after you have reviewed the fields. Confirmed fields enter the comparison; unsupported lines stay unresolved.

A small model trained on synthetic action phrases suggests the action; rules identify the other fields. This is an experimental extraction aid, not a clinically validated interpretation.
SOURCE RECORD

Add a record

Supported format & limitations

Start with Start, Continue, Change, or Stop. For instructions other than Stop, include the medicine name, written amount (mg, mcg, g, mL, or units), optional oral/topical route, and frequency: once daily, twice daily, three times daily, once weekly, or as needed.

Example: Continue Metformin 500 mg orally twice daily.

Names are matched exactly, ignoring case. Brand aliases, tablet counts, tapers, combination products, durations, effective dates, and handwriting are not interpreted. Unread lines remain flagged. The written amount is not automatically classified as product strength or administered dose.

Only use fictional or appropriately de-identified records in this prototype. Nothing is sent to an AI service.
WELCOME TO MEDDELTA

Make sense of the changes.

MedDelta puts dated medication instructions side by side so a reviewer can see what is explained and what is still unclear.

  1. Explore the example. Open any medication to see its timeline and original evidence.
  2. Review the extraction. Choose “Review natural wording”, open Source records, and check the suggested fields against the original text.
  3. Try a change. Edit a source record or import a typed PDF. Use “Try a sample PDF” to explore without your own documents.
  4. Capture a review. Add a note to a finding, then export the complete report.
An honest first version

The comparison engine uses explicit rules. Expanded extraction uses a small local action classifier trained on synthetic phrases, plus field rules. A reviewer must confirm expanded suggestions. This is not clinically validated and does not recommend treatment. Unsupported text remains flagged.

Record dates order the timeline; treatment effective dates are not inferred. Explicit changes remain evidence from a document, not proof of an appropriate regimen. A reviewer note marks review activity without certifying safety.

Work stays in this browser tab and resets on reload. Export before leaving. This free prototype needs no API key.
